raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

First part of the "direct Metal semantic ops for eager" item in the Apple Silicon roadmap (#32321): RMSNorm on the Torch MPS eager path. SiLU-and-mul follows in a separate PR.

Today `RMSNorm` has no MPS path, so on Apple Silicon it runs `forward_native`: an fp32 upcast, `pow`, `mean`, `rsqrt` and two multiplies, each a separate MPS kernel with its own fp32 intermediate. This PR replaces that with one Metal kernel per call.

## Modifications

- `fused_op.py`: add an `"mps"` platform key, so `BaseFusedOp` dispatches to `forward_mps` on Apple Silicon. Ops that don't define `forward_mps` still fall back to `forward_native`, so nothing else changes.
- `kernels/ops/layernorm/rmsnorm_mps.py` (new): RMSNorm and fused add + RMSNorm, compiled with `torch.mps.compile_shader`. One threadgroup per row. The sum of squares and the residual add are done in fp32, like `forward_native`; only the stores round to the input dtype. Supports fp32, fp16 and bf16. Inputs are never modified; the fused variant returns `(out, x + residual)`.
- `layernorm.py`: `RMSNorm.forward_mps` uses the kernel for the plain variant. Everything else goes to `forward_native`: `post_residual_addition`, `var_hidden_size`, `cast_x_before_out_mul`, `fp32_residual`, `override_orig_dtype`, and mismatched dtypes or shapes.
- `test_rmsnorm_mps.py` (new, registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mps`): parity against `forward_native` and a dispatch test.

## Accuracy Tests

`test_rmsnorm_mps.py` compares against `RMSNorm.forward_native` for fp32/fp16/bf16, with and without residual, on shapes `(1, 7)`, `(3, 64)`, `(5, 1000)`, `(2, 3, 2048)`, `(4, 4100)`. The odd widths leave idle threads in the last SIMD group, and 4100 makes each thread loop over several elements.
- Normalized output: `atol`/`rtol` of 1e-5 (fp32), 2e-3 (fp16), 1.6e-2 (bf16).
- Residual sum: bit-exact.
- Inputs are checked to be unchanged.

The dispatch test checks that the plain variant calls the kernel exactly once, and that `fp32_residual`, `var_hidden_size` and a dtype mismatch go to the native path.

This only touches the MPS eager path. CUDA, ROCm, NPU, XPU, MUSA and CPU dispatch is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Op-level microbenchmark on Apple M2 Max (64 GB), macOS 27.2, PyTorch 2.13.0. Each number is the median of 5 runs of 200 calls after warmup, with `torch.mps.synchronize()` around each run. It compares `RMSNorm.forward_native` against `forward_mps`, in µs per call, bf16:

| hidden | tokens | native | Metal | native, +res | Metal, +res |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 1 | 43.4 | 12.0 (3.6x) | 56.4 | 14.3 (3.9x) |
| 4096 | 16 | 58.0 | 12.2 (4.7x) | 75.1 | 13.8 (5.5x) |
| 4096 | 256 | 285.4 | 22.1 (12.9x) | 355.1 | 30.9 (11.5x) |
| 4096 | 2048 | 2418.8 | 113.8 (21.3x) | 2820.4 | 234.6 (12.0x) |
| 8192 | 1 | 43.1 | 14.2 (3.0x) | 54.4 | 15.6 (3.5x) |
| 8192 | 2048 | 4505.5 | 197.4 (22.8x) | 5664.9 | 460.0 (12.3x) |

Across hidden 2048/4096/8192, tokens 1/16/256/2048, and fp16 or bf16, the Metal path is 3.0x to 26x faster than native in every case. Decode-sized calls (1 token) go from about 40–70 µs to 11–16 µs.

These are op-level numbers. I haven't measured end-to-end serving throughput on MPS with this change.

+"""RMSNorm and fused add + RMSNorm for the Torch MPS eager path (Metal JIT)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+from typing import Optional, Tuple, Union
+
+import torch
+
+# One threadgroup normalizes one row. Every reduction and the residual sum run
+# in fp32, matching RMSNorm.forward_native; only the stores round to T.
+_METAL_SOURCE = """
+#include <metal_stdlib>
+using namespace metal;
+
+template <typename T>
+inline float row_inv_rms(
+    device const T* x, device const T* residual, uint n, float eps,
+    uint tid, uint group_size, uint lane, uint simd_id,
+    threadgroup float* partials
+) {
+    float sum = 0.0f;
+    for (uint i = tid; i < n; i += group_size) {
+        float h = float(x[i]);
+        if (residual != nullptr) {
+            h += float(residual[i]);
+        }
+        sum += h * h;
+    }
+    sum = simd_sum(sum);
+    if (lane == 0) {
+        partials[simd_id] = sum;
+    }
+    threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
+    if (simd_id == 0) {
+        uint num_simds = (group_size + 31) / 32;
+        sum = lane < num_simds ? partials[lane] : 0.0f;
+        sum = simd_sum(sum);
+        if (lane == 0) {
+            partials[0] = rsqrt(sum / float(n) + eps);
+        }
+    }
+    threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
+    return partials[0];
+}
+
+#define DEFINE_RMSNORM(T, NAME)                                               \\
+kernel void rmsnorm_##NAME(                                                   \\
+    device const T* x [[buffer(0)]],                                          \\
+    device const T* weight [[buffer(1)]],                                     \\
+    device T* out [[buffer(2)]],                                              \\
+    constant float& eps [[buffer(3)]],                                        \\
+    constant uint& n [[buffer(4)]],                                           \\
+    uint row [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]],                                \\
+    uint tid [[thread_position_in_threadgroup]],                              \\
+    uint group_size [[threads_per_threadgroup]],                              \\
+    uint lane [[thread_index_in_simdgroup]],                                  \\
+    uint simd_id [[simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup]]                           \\
+) {                                                                           \\
+    threadgroup float partials[32];                                           \\
+    x += row * n;                                                             \\
+    out += row * n;                                                           \\
+    float inv_rms = row_inv_rms<T>(                                           \\
+        x, nullptr, n, eps, tid, group_size, lane, simd_id, partials);        \\
+    for (uint i = tid; i < n; i += group_size) {                              \\
+        out[i] = T(float(x[i]) * inv_rms * float(weight[i]));                 \\
+    }                                                                         \\
+}                                                                             \\
+                                                                              \\
+kernel void fused_add_rmsnorm_##NAME(                                         \\
+    device const T* x [[buffer(0)]],                                          \\
+    device const T* residual [[buffer(1)]],                                   \\
+    device const T* weight [[buffer(2)]],                                     \\
+    device T* out [[buffer(3)]],                                              \\
+    device T* residual_out [[buffer(4)]],                                     \\
+    constant float& eps [[buffer(5)]],                                        \\
+    constant uint& n [[buffer(6)]],                                           \\
+    uint row [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]],                                \\
+    uint tid [[thread_position_in_threadgroup]],                              \\
+    uint group_size [[threads_per_threadgroup]],                              \\
+    uint lane [[thread_index_in_simdgroup]],                                  \\
+    uint simd_id [[simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup]]                           \\
+) {                                                                           \\
+    threadgroup float partials[32];                                           \\
+    x += row * n;                                                             \\
+    residual += row * n;                                                      \\
+    out += row * n;                                                           \\
+    residual_out += row * n;                                                  \\
+    float inv_rms = row_inv_rms<T>(                                           \\
+        x, residual, n, eps, tid, group_size, lane, simd_id, partials);       \\
+    for (uint i = tid; i < n; i += group_size) {                              \\
+        float h = float(x[i]) + float(residual[i]);                           \\
+        residual_out[i] = T(h);                                               \\
+        out[i] = T(h * inv_rms * float(weight[i]));                           \\
+    }                                                                         \\
+}
+
+DEFINE_RMSNORM(float, float)
+DEFINE_RMSNORM(half, half)
+DEFINE_RMSNORM(bfloat, bfloat)
+"""
+
+_DTYPE_SUFFIX = {
+    torch.float32: "float",
+    torch.float16: "half",
+    torch.bfloat16: "bfloat",
+}
+_MAX_GROUP_SIZE = 1024
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _library():
+    return torch.mps.compile_shader(_METAL_SOURCE)
+
+
+def rmsnorm_mps_supported(
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, residual: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether :func:`rmsnorm_mps` handles these operands."""
+    return (
+        x.device.type == "mps"
+        and x.dtype in _DTYPE_SUFFIX
+        and x.numel() > 0
+        and weight.dtype == x.dtype
+        and weight.shape == (x.shape[-1],)
+        and (
+            residual is None
+            or (residual.dtype == x.dtype and residual.shape == x.shape)
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def rmsnorm_mps(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    eps: float,
+    residual: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+) -> Union[torch.Tensor, Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+    """``x * rsqrt(mean(x**2) + eps) * weight`` over the last dim.
+
+    With ``residual``, normalizes ``x + residual`` and also returns that sum.
+    Neither input is modified. Callers check :func:`rmsnorm_mps_supported`.
+    """
+    hidden_size = x.shape[-1]
+    rows = x.numel() // hidden_size
+    x = x.contiguous()
+    weight = weight.contiguous()
+    suffix = _DTYPE_SUFFIX[x.dtype]
+    # A multiple of the 32-wide SIMD group, so every simd_sum lane is in range.
+    group_size = min(_MAX_GROUP_SIZE, (hidden_size + 31) // 32 * 32)
+    launch = dict(threads=rows * group_size, group_size=group_size)
+
+    out = torch.empty_like(x)
+    if residual is None:
+        getattr(_library(), f"rmsnorm_{suffix}")(
+            x, weight, out, eps, hidden_size, **launch
+        )
+        return out
+
+    residual_out = torch.empty_like(x)
+    getattr(_library(), f"fused_add_rmsnorm_{suffix}")(
+        x, residual.contiguous(), weight, out, residual_out, eps, hidden_size, **launch
+    )
+    return out, residual_out

@@ -945,6 +945,31 @@ def forward_cpu(
         else:
             return self.forward_native(x, residual, post_residual_addition)
 
+    def forward_mps(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        residual: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        post_residual_addition: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+        quant_linear: Optional[nn.Module] = None,
+    ) -> Union[torch.Tensor, Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:

+            rmsnorm_mps,
+            rmsnorm_mps_supported,
+        )
+
+        # The Metal kernel covers the plain variant; the rest stays native.
+        if (
+            post_residual_addition is None
+            and self.variance_size_override is None
+            and not self.cast_x_before_out_mul
+            and not self.fp32_residual
+            and self.override_orig_dtype is None

+        ):

+        return self.forward_native(x, residual, post_residual_addition)
+
     def forward_xpu(
         self,
         x: torch.Tensor,

@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_mps_ci
+
+register_mps_ci(est_time=10, suite="stage-a-unit-test-mps")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.backends.mps.is_available(), reason="requires Apple MPS"
+)
+
+DEVICE = "mps"
+EPS = 1e-6
+# One output ulp: fp32 differs only by reduction order, half types by rounding.
+TOLERANCE = {
+    torch.float32: dict(atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-5),
+    torch.float16: dict(atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3),
+    torch.bfloat16: dict(atol=1.6e-2, rtol=1.6e-2),
+}
+# Odd widths leave idle threads in the last SIMD group; 4100 > 1024 makes
+# each thread loop over several elements.
+SHAPES = [(1, 7), (3, 64), (5, 1000), (2, 3, 2048), (4, 4100)]
+
+
+def _make_norm(hidden_size, dtype, **kwargs):
+    from sglang.srt.layers.layernorm import RMSNorm
+
+    norm = RMSNorm(hidden_size, eps=EPS, **kwargs).to(device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        norm.weight.normal_()
+    return norm
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", list(TOLERANCE))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_residual", [False, True])
+def test_rmsnorm_mps_matches_native(dtype, shape, with_residual):
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.rmsnorm_mps import rmsnorm_mps
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    norm = _make_norm(shape[-1], dtype)
+    x = torch.randn(shape, device=DEVICE, dtype=dtype)
+    residual = torch.randn_like(x) if with_residual else None
+    inputs = (x.clone(), None if residual is None else residual.clone())
+
+    expected = norm.forward_native(x, residual)
+    actual = rmsnorm_mps(x, norm.weight, EPS, residual)
+
+    if with_residual:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual[0], expected[0], **TOLERANCE[dtype])
+        # Both paths round the same fp32 sum, so the residual is exact.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual[1], expected[1], atol=0, rtol=0)
+    else:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, **TOLERANCE[dtype])
+    torch.testing.assert_close(x, inputs[0], atol=0, rtol=0)
+    if residual is not None:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(residual, inputs[1], atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+def test_rmsnorm_dispatches_to_mps_kernel(monkeypatch):
+    import sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.rmsnorm_mps as rmsnorm_mps_module
+
+    calls = []
+    kernel = rmsnorm_mps_module.rmsnorm_mps
+
+    def counting_kernel(*args, **kwargs):
+        calls.append(args)
+        return kernel(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(rmsnorm_mps_module, "rmsnorm_mps", counting_kernel)
+    x = torch.randn(2, 64, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+    _make_norm(64, torch.bfloat16)(x)
+    assert len(calls) == 1
+
+    # Variants the kernel does not implement must take the native path.
+    _make_norm(64, torch.bfloat16, fp32_residual=True)(x, torch.randn_like(x))
+    _make_norm(64, torch.bfloat16, var_hidden_size=32)(x)
+    _make_norm(64, torch.bfloat16)(x.float())
+    assert len(calls) == 1
